hints: Express the integrand using negative indices as $2x^{-2}$ before integrating.
Apply the power rule $\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}$ to obtain an expression of the form $-2x^{-1}$.
Evaluate the definite integral between the limits $3$ and $\infty$, noting that $-\frac{2}{x} \to 0$ as $x \to \infty$.
walkthrough:
Express the integrand with a negative index and integrate with respect to $x$:
$$\int \frac{2}{x^2}\,dx = \int 2x^{-2}\,dx = \frac{2x^{-1}}{-1} = -2x^{-1} = -\frac{2}{x}$$

Apply the limits of integration from $x = 3$ to $\infty$, setting up the limit expression:
$$\int_3^\infty \frac{2}{x^2}\,dx = \left[ -\frac{2}{x} \right]_3^\infty = \lim_{b\to\infty} \left( -\frac{2}{b} - \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) \right)$$

Evaluate the limit as $b \to \infty$, using the fact that $-\frac{2}{b} \to 0$:
$$0 + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$$
